title: Food Fermentation, Fermented Food Products and Beverages
shortDescription: Starter cultures, the biochemistry of fermentation and a tour of fermented foods.
genZNote: Fermentation is controlled spoilage with a good PR team. Idli batter, dahi, vinegar — all microbes doing free labour.

sections.heading: Principles
bullets: Fermentation: microbial/enzymatic conversion of carbohydrates to acids, alcohol or gas under (mostly) anaerobic conditions; improves safety (acid, alcohol, bacteriocins), flavour, digestibility and nutrients (B vitamins).
Lactic acid bacteria (LAB): Lactobacillus, Lactococcus, Streptococcus thermophilus, Leuconostoc, Pediococcus.

Yeasts: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (alcoholic fermentation, leavening); moulds: Aspergillus oryzae (koji), Rhizopus oligosporus (tempeh); acetic acid bacteria: Acetobacter (vinegar); Propionibacterium (Swiss cheese eyes).
Starter cultures (single, multiple, mixed; mesophilic vs thermophilic); backslopping in traditional practice.

sections.heading: Products
sections.body: Beverage steps: beer (malting, mashing, boiling with hops, fermentation); wine (crushing, fermentation, ageing); distilled spirits require distillation. FSSAI sets standards for alcoholic beverages and non-alcoholic fermented drinks; fermented foods are permitted when safe and labelled correctly.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Food fermentation uses microorganisms to transform raw materials into products with improved flavour, safety, shelf life and nutrition.
keyFacts: Vinegar: yeast → alcohol → acetic acid by Acetobacter.

highYieldFacts: Homofermentative LAB produce mainly lactic acid.
commonTraps: Do not confuse fermentation with spoilage.
